\chapter{Communication Complexity — Public Coin One Way}
%%% generated by the blueprint pipeline from TCSlib.CommunicationComplexity.NewmanTheorem.PublicCoinOneWay
\section{Overview}

This module defines one-way public-coin protocols and their $\varepsilon$-error
communication complexity.  A public-coin protocol is modelled as a deterministic
one-way protocol whose input spaces are augmented with a shared randomness type
$\Omega$; correctness is measured by the probability (over the shared randomness)
that the protocol's output disagrees with the target function.

%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%
\section{Declarations}

\begin{definition}[One-way public-coin protocol]
\lean{CommunicationComplexity.PublicCoin.OneWay.Protocol}
\statementsource{roughgarden-cc-oneway}{
  pdf-043896d6545f-p002-b003,
  pdf-043896d6545f-p010-b002
}
\label{CommunicationComplexity.PublicCoin.OneWay.Protocol}
\leanok
\uses{CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.OneWay.Protocol}
A one-way public-coin protocol over shared randomness type $\Omega$ and
input types $X$, $Y$ with output type $\alpha$ is defined as a deterministic
one-way protocol whose Alice-input is $\Omega \times X$ and whose Bob-input is
$\Omega \times Y$.  The shared randomness $\omega \in \Omega$ is thus treated as
a component of both players' inputs.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Protocol execution with shared randomness]
\lean{CommunicationComplexity.PublicCoin.OneWay.Protocol.rrun}
\statementsource{roughgarden-cc-oneway}{
  pdf-043896d6545f-p002-b003,
  pdf-043896d6545f-p010-b002
}
\label{CommunicationComplexity.PublicCoin.OneWay.Protocol.rrun}
\leanok
\uses{CommunicationComplexity.PublicCoin.OneWay.Protocol}
Given a protocol $p$, inputs $x \in X$, $y \in Y$, and a shared random string
$\omega \in \Omega$, the execution $\mathrm{rrun}(p, x, y, \omega)$ runs $p$ on
the joint inputs $(\omega, x)$ for Alice and $(\omega, y)$ for Bob, returning
the decoded output $p.\mathrm{decode}(p.\mathrm{send}(\omega, x),\,(\omega, y))$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[$\varepsilon$-approximate computation]
\lean{CommunicationComplexity.PublicCoin.OneWay.Protocol.ApproxComputes}
\statementsource{roughgarden-cc-oneway}{
  pdf-043896d6545f-p010-b003,
  pdf-043896d6545f-p002-b004
}
\label{CommunicationComplexity.PublicCoin.OneWay.Protocol.ApproxComputes}
\leanok
\uses{CommunicationComplexity.PublicCoin.OneWay.Protocol, CommunicationComplexity.PublicCoin.OneWay.Protocol.rrun}
A protocol $p$ $\varepsilon$-computes a function $f : X \to Y \to \alpha$ if
for every input pair $(x, y)$ the measure of the set of shared strings on which
$p$ errs is at most $\varepsilon$:
\[
  \forall x,\, y,\quad
  \mu\bigl(\{\omega \mid p.\mathrm{rrun}(x,y,\omega) \ne f(x,y)\}\bigr) \;\le\; \varepsilon.
\]
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[$\varepsilon$-error one-way public-coin communication complexity]
\lean{CommunicationComplexity.PublicCoin.OneWay.communicationComplexity}
\statementsource{roughgarden-cc-oneway}{
  pdf-043896d6545f-p002-b004,
  pdf-043896d6545f-p011-b002
}
\label{CommunicationComplexity.PublicCoin.OneWay.communicationComplexity}
\leanok
\uses{CommunicationComplexity.CoinTape, CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.OneWay.Protocol.cost, CommunicationComplexity.PublicCoin.OneWay.Protocol, CommunicationComplexity.PublicCoin.OneWay.Protocol.ApproxComputes}
The $\varepsilon$-error one-way public-coin communication complexity of
$f : X \to Y \to \alpha$ is the infimum (in $\mathbb{N}_\infty$) of the
one-way message cost $p.\mathrm{cost}$ over all $n \in \mathbb{N}$ and all
protocols $p$ over the coin-tape space $\mathrm{CoinTape}(n)$ that
$\varepsilon$-compute $f$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Upper-bound characterisation of public-coin communication complexity]
\lean{CommunicationComplexity.PublicCoin.OneWay.communicationComplexity_le_iff}
\label{CommunicationComplexity.PublicCoin.OneWay.communicationComplexity_le_iff}
\leanok
\uses{CommunicationComplexity.CoinTape, CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.OneWay.Protocol.cost, CommunicationComplexity.Internal.enat_iInf_le_coe_iff, CommunicationComplexity.PublicCoin.OneWay.Protocol, CommunicationComplexity.PublicCoin.OneWay.Protocol.ApproxComputes, CommunicationComplexity.PublicCoin.OneWay.communicationComplexity}
\difficulty{2}
Fix a function $f : X \to Y \to \alpha$, a real error bound $\varepsilon$, and a natural
number $m$. Then the $\varepsilon$-error one-way public-coin communication complexity of
$f$ is at most $m$ (as an element of $\bbn_\infty$) if and only if there exist a length
$n \in \bbn$ and a one-way public-coin protocol $p$ over the coin-tape space
$\mathrm{CoinTape}(n)$ such that $p$ $\varepsilon$-computes $f$ and the bit cost of $p$
is at most $m$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Lower-bound characterisation of one-way public-coin communication complexity]
\lean{CommunicationComplexity.PublicCoin.OneWay.le_communicationComplexity_iff}
\label{CommunicationComplexity.PublicCoin.OneWay.le_communicationComplexity_iff}
\leanok
\uses{CommunicationComplexity.CoinTape, CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.OneWay.Protocol.cost, CommunicationComplexity.PublicCoin.OneWay.Protocol, CommunicationComplexity.PublicCoin.OneWay.Protocol.ApproxComputes, CommunicationComplexity.PublicCoin.OneWay.communicationComplexity}
\difficulty{2}
Let $f : X \to Y \to \alpha$ be a function, let $\varepsilon \in \bbr$, and let $m \in
\bbn$. Then $m$ is a lower bound for the $\varepsilon$-error one-way public-coin
communication complexity of $f$, in the sense that $m \le \mathrm{CC}(f,\varepsilon)$ as
elements of $\bbn_\infty$, if and only if every protocol $p$ over a coin tape
$\mathrm{CoinTape}(n)$ of any length $n \in \bbn$ that $\varepsilon$-computes $f$ has
bit cost at least $m$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Monotonicity of communication complexity in the error tolerance]
\lean{CommunicationComplexity.PublicCoin.OneWay.communicationComplexity_mono}
\label{CommunicationComplexity.PublicCoin.OneWay.communicationComplexity_mono}
\leanok
\uses{CommunicationComplexity.PublicCoin.OneWay.communicationComplexity, CommunicationComplexity.PublicCoin.OneWay.communicationComplexity_le_iff}
\difficulty{4}
Fix a function $f : X \to Y \to \alpha$ and real error tolerances $\varepsilon',
\varepsilon$ with $\varepsilon' \le \varepsilon$. Then the $\varepsilon$-error one-way
public-coin communication complexity of $f$ is at most its $\varepsilon'$-error one-way
public-coin communication complexity, where each such complexity is the infimum (in
$\bbn \cup \{\infty\}$) of the bit cost over all coin-tape lengths $n$ and all one-way
public-coin protocols that compute $f$ to the corresponding error tolerance. In other
words, relaxing the permitted error can only decrease (or leave unchanged) the required
communication.
\end{theorem}
